title: Find Second Largest Element
problemStatement: Given an array of integers `arr`, write a function `findSecondLargest(arr)` that returns the second largest element in the array. If no such element exists (e.g. all elements are equal or the array has fewer than 2 distinct values), return -1.
description: The array can contain duplicate values. The second largest must be strictly smaller than the largest value.
constraints:
1 <= arr.length <= 10^5
-10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
outputFormat: A single integer — the second largest element, or -1 if it does not exist.

examples.explanation: The largest element is 35 and the second largest is 34.
All elements are equal, so there is no second largest element.

explanation: Track the largest and second largest values in a single pass. If every value equals the largest, return -1.

title: Sum of Prime Digits
problemStatement: Given a number represented as a string `numStr`, write a function `sumOfPrimeDigits(numStr)` that returns the sum of all digits which are prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7). Non-prime digits are ignored.
description: Treat the input purely as a string of digits. The result is the sum of the digit values 2, 3, 5 and 7 wherever they appear.
constraints:
1 <= numStr.length <= 10^5
numStr contains only digits '0'-'9'
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
inputFormat: A single string containing digits only.
outputFormat: A single integer — the sum of the prime digits.

examples.explanation: None of the digits are prime, so the sum is 0.

explanation: Iterate over each character, convert it to an integer, and add it to the total only if it is 2, 3, 5 or 7.

title: Reverse Words in a String
problemStatement: Given an input string `s`, write a function `reverseWords(s)` that reverses the order of the words. A word is a sequence of non-space characters. Words in `s` are separated by at least one space. Return the words in reverse order joined by a single space.
description: Leading and trailing spaces are ignored, and multiple spaces between words are collapsed into one in the output.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^4
s contains printable ASCII characters and spaces
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)
outputFormat: A single string with words reversed and separated by a single space.

examples.explanation: The words are reversed in order: blue, is, sky, the.
Extra spaces are trimmed from both ends and between words.

explanation: Split the string on whitespace, filter out empty tokens, reverse the list and join with a single space.

title: Check Leap Year
problemStatement: Given an integer `year`, write a function `isLeapYear(year)` that returns `true` if the year is a leap year, and `false` otherwise.
description: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but NOT divisible by 100.
constraints:
1 <= year <= 10^5
Time: O(1)
Space: O(1)
explanation: Return true if (year % 400 === 0) || (year % 4 === 0 && year % 100 !== 0).

title: Count Vowels and Consonants
problemStatement: Given a string `s`, write a function `countVowelsAndConsonants(s)` that returns an array `[vowelCount, consonantCount]`. Ignore non-alphabetic characters (digits, spaces, punctuation). Case-insensitive.
description: Vowels are 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' (both lowercase and uppercase). Consonants are all other alphabetic letters.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^5
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
outputFormat: An array of two integers [vowels, consonants].

examples.explanation: Vowels: e, o, o (3). Consonants: H, l, l, W, r, l, d (7).

explanation: Iterate through the string, check if character is a letter, and classify as vowel or consonant.

title: Check Armstrong Number
problemStatement: Given a positive integer `n`, write a function `isArmstrong(n)` that returns `true` if `n` is an Armstrong number (Narcissistic number), and `false` otherwise.
description: An Armstrong number of k digits is an integer such that the sum of its digits each raised to the power of k equals the number itself.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 10^8
Time: O(log N)
Space: O(1)
explanation: Count the number of digits k, compute the sum of digit^k, and compare with n.

title: Move Zeroes to End
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, write a function `moveZeroes(nums)` that moves all `0`s to the end of the array while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements. Return the modified array.
description: Operate in-place or return a new array with all zeroes placed at the end without altering non-zero sequence.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1) auxiliary
outputFormat: An array of integers with all zeroes moved to the end.

examples.explanation: Non-zero elements 1, 3, 12 keep order, two 0s moved to the end.

explanation: Use a pointer to track the insertion index of non-zero elements. Fill the remainder with zeroes.

title: Sum of Array Except Minimum and Maximum
problemStatement: Given an array of numbers `arr`, write a function `sumExceptMinMax(arr)` that returns the sum of all elements excluding the smallest and largest values. If there are duplicates of the minimum or maximum value, exclude only one instance of minimum and one instance of maximum. If array length is less than 3, return 0.
description: Calculates total sum minus one minimum element and minus one maximum element.
constraints:
1 <= arr.length <= 10^5
-10^5 <= arr[i] <= 10^5
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
explanation: Sum the array in one pass while tracking min and max. Return sum - min - max.

title: Check Palindrome String
problemStatement: Given a string `s`, write a function `isPalindrome(s)` that returns `true` if `s` is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring cases, and `false` otherwise.
description: A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^5
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)

examples.input: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

explanation: Use two pointers moving inward, skipping non-alphanumeric characters and comparing lowercase versions.

publicTestCases.input: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

title: Find Missing Number in 1 to N
problemStatement: Given an array `nums` containing `n` distinct numbers in the range `[0, n]`, return the only number in the range that is missing from the array.
description: All numbers from 0 to n appear in nums except one.
constraints:
n == nums.length
1 <= n <= 10^4
0 <= nums[i] <= n
All numbers in nums are unique.
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
explanation: Expected sum is n*(n+1)/2. The missing number is expected sum - actual sum.

title: Majority Element
problemStatement: Given an array `nums` of size `n`, return the majority element. The majority element is the element that appears more than `n / 2` times. You may assume that the majority element always exists in the array.
description: Find the element appearing > floor(n/2) times.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 5 * 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
explanation: Use Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm: maintain a candidate and count.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum (Kadane's Algorithm)
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.
description: A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)

examples.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum = 6.

explanation: Use Kadane's Algorithm: maxCurrent = Math.max(nums[i], maxCurrent + nums[i]), maxGlobal = Math.max(maxGlobal, maxCurrent).

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problemStatement: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
description: A substring is a contiguous non-empty sequence of characters within a string.
constraints:
0 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4
s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.
Time: O(N)
Space: O(min(N, M)) where M is character set size

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with the length of 3.
The answer is "b", with the length of 1.
The answer is "wke", with the length of 3.

explanation: Use a sliding window with a hash map storing the last seen index of each character.

title: String Compression (Run-Length Encoding)
problemStatement: Given a string `s` of consecutive characters, write a function `compressString(s)` that returns the compressed string using run-length encoding. For each consecutive group of identical characters, append the character followed by its count. If the count is 1, still include the count 1.
description: Example: "aabcccccaaa" becomes "a2b1c5a3".
constraints:
0 <= s.length <= 10^5
s contains alphabetic characters.
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)
explanation: Iterate with a counter tracking consecutive identical characters, appending char and count upon change.

title: Rotate Array Right by K Steps
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, rotate the array to the right by `k` steps, where `k` is non-negative. Return the rotated array.
description: Elements shifted past the end wrap around to the beginning.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
-2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1
0 <= k <= 10^5
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1) auxiliary
inputFormat: An array nums and integer k.
explanation: Normalize k = k % n. Reverse whole array, reverse first k elements, reverse remaining n-k elements.

title: Two Sum - Indices of Target Pair
problemStatement: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices in increasing order.
description: Find [i, j] such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target and i < j.
constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
-10^9 <= target <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)
inputFormat: An array nums and integer target.
explanation: Store complement (target - nums[i]) in a hash map mapping value to index.

title: Valid Parentheses / Balanced Brackets
problemStatement: Given a string `s` containing just the characters `'('`, `')'`, `'{'`, `'}'`, `'['` and `']'`, determine if the input string is valid. Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets in the correct order.
description: An input string is valid if every open bracket has a corresponding closing bracket of the same type.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^4
s consists of parentheses only '()[]{}'.
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)
explanation: Push opening brackets onto a stack. When encountering a closing bracket, pop and ensure match.

title: Next Permutation
problemStatement: A permutation of an array of integers is an arrangement of its members into a sequence. Given an array of integers `nums`, find the next lexicographically greater permutation of numbers. If no such permutation is possible (it is in descending order), rearrange it to the lowest possible order (sorted in ascending order). Return the modified array.
description: Find the next lexicographical permutation in-place or return the transformed array.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 100
0 <= nums[i] <= 100
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
outputFormat: An array representing the next permutation.

examples.explanation: 3,2,1 is the largest, wrapped around to 1,2,3.

explanation: 1. Find first decreasing element from right (i). 2. Find element just larger than nums[i] from right (j). 3. Swap nums[i] and nums[j]. 4. Reverse subarray from i+1 to end.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problemStatement: Given the array `nums` after the possible rotation and an integer `target`, return the index of `target` if it is in `nums`, or `-1` if it is not in `nums`. You must write an algorithm with `O(log n)` runtime complexity.
description: An array sorted in ascending order is rotated at an unknown pivot. Find target index.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 5000
-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
All values of nums are unique.
Time: O(log N)
Space: O(1)
inputFormat: An array nums and integer target.
explanation: At each step of binary search, one half (left or right) is guaranteed to be sorted. Check if target lies in the sorted half.

title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
problemStatement: Given an array of `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]`, merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.
description: Intervals [a, b] and [c, d] overlap if c <= b.
constraints:
1 <= intervals.length <= 10^4
intervals[i].length == 2
0 <= start_i <= end_i <= 10^4
Time: O(N log N)
Space: O(N)
explanation: Sort intervals by start time. Iterate through: if current start <= previous end, merge (end = max(prev.end, curr.end)), else add new interval.

title: Product of Array Except Self
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`. You must write an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and without using the division operation.
description: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums fits in a 32-bit integer.
constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^5
-30 <= nums[i] <= 30
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1) auxiliary
outputFormat: An array of integers where answer[i] is product except nums[i].

examples.explanation: Prefix products combined with suffix products.
Zero at index 2 causes other elements to be 0.

explanation: Construct prefix products in one pass, then compute suffix products in reverse pass multiplying into result.

title: Group Anagrams
problemStatement: Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order. Within each group, preserve relative order or sort.
description: An Anagram is a word formed by rearranging the letters of a different word.
constraints:
1 <= strs.length <= 10^4
0 <= strs[i].length <= 100
strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
Time: O(N * K log K)
Space: O(N * K)
outputFormat: A 2D array of grouped anagram strings.
explanation: Use the sorted string as the hash map key, grouping original strings as map values.

title: Find Kth Largest Element in Array
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k`th largest element in the array. Note that it is the `k`th largest element in the sorted order, not the `k`th distinct element.
description: Can you solve it without sorting in O(N) average time using Quickselect or Min-Heap?
constraints:
1 <= k <= nums.length <= 10^5
-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
Time: O(N log K) or O(N) avg
Space: O(K)
inputFormat: An array nums and integer k.
explanation: Use a min-heap of size k, or Quickselect partitioning around a pivot.

title: Trapping Rain Water
problemStatement: Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is `1`, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
description: Each bar height determines water bounded between left and right walls.
constraints:
n == height.length
1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4
0 <= height[i] <= 10^5
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
inputFormat: An array of non-negative integers height.
outputFormat: A single integer representing total trapped water units.

examples.explanation: 6 total units of rain water trapped.

explanation: Two pointers left=0, right=n-1 with maxLeft and maxRight tracking bounding boundary elevations.

title: Minimum Cost of Connecting Ropes
problemStatement: Given an array `ropes` representing the lengths of different ropes, connect all ropes into one rope with the minimum total cost. The cost to connect two ropes is equal to the sum of their lengths.
description: Always connecting the two shortest available ropes minimizes cumulative cost (Huffman coding principle).
constraints:
1 <= ropes.length <= 10^5
1 <= ropes[i] <= 10^4
Time: O(N log N)
Space: O(N)
inputFormat: An array of positive integers ropes.
outputFormat: A single integer total minimum cost.

examples.explanation: Connect 2+3=5 (cost 5). Array [4, 5, 6]. Connect 4+5=9 (cost 9). Array [6, 9]. Connect 6+9=15 (cost 15). Total = 5 + 9 + 15 = 29.

explanation: Insert all rope lengths into a Min-Heap. Repeatedly extract two smallest, sum them, add to total cost, and re-insert the sum.

title: Find Longest Common Prefix
problemStatement: Write a function `longestCommonPrefix(strs)` to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string `""`.
description: Compare characters at each index across all strings in the array.
constraints:
1 <= strs.length <= 200
0 <= strs[i].length <= 200
strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
Time: O(S) where S is sum of all chars
Space: O(1)
explanation: Take first string as reference, compare char by char across all other strings until mismatch.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problemStatement: Given a string `s`, return the longest palindromic substring in `s`.
description: A string is palindromic if it reads the same forward and backward.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s consist of only digits and English letters.
Time: O(N^2)
Space: O(1) auxiliary
outputFormat: A single string containing the longest palindromic substring.
explanation: Expand around each possible center (both 1-char center for odd length and 2-char center for even length).

title: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
problemStatement: Given `W` (maximum capacity of knapsack) and two arrays `values` and `weights` of size `N`, find the maximum total value subset of `values` such that total weight does not exceed `W`. You cannot break items (0/1).
description: Classic 0/1 knapsack with weights and values.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000
1 <= W <= 1000
1 <= weights[i], values[i] <= 1000
Time: O(N * W)
Space: O(W)
inputFormat: An integer W, array values, and array weights.

examples.explanation: Pick items with weights 20 and 30, total value = 100 + 120 = 220.
Pick items with weight 4 and 3 (total weight 7 <= 10), value = 40 + 50 = 90.

explanation: dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - weight[i]] + value[i]) in reverse loop.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problemStatement: Given two sorted arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of size `m` and `n` respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays. The overall run time complexity should be `O(log (m+n))`.
description: Partition both arrays such that left half has equal elements to right half and left elements <= right elements.
constraints:
nums1.length == m
nums2.length == n
0 <= m <= 1000
0 <= n <= 1000
1 <= m + n <= 2000
Time: O(log(min(m, n)))
Space: O(1)
inputFormat: Two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2.
explanation: Perform binary search on the shorter array's partition index. Validate left1 <= right2 and left2 <= right1.

title: Coin Change - Minimum Number of Coins
problemStatement: You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount` representing a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return `-1`.
description: You may assume that you have an infinite number of each kind of coin.
constraints:
1 <= coins.length <= 12
1 <= coins[i] <= 2^31 - 1
0 <= amount <= 10^4
Time: O(amount * |coins|)
Space: O(amount)
inputFormat: An array coins and integer amount.
explanation: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1) for each coin <= i.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
description: A subsequence is a sequence that can be derived from an array by deleting some or no elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 2500
-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
Time: O(N log N) or O(N^2)
Space: O(N)

examples.explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2, 3, 7, 101], therefore length is 4.

explanation: Use Patience Sorting / Tails array with binary search (O(N log N)).

title: Word Break Problem
problemStatement: Given a string `s` and a dictionary of strings `wordDict`, return `true` if `s` can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words.
description: The same word in the dictionary may be reused multiple times in the segmentation.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 300
1 <= wordDict.length <= 1000
1 <= wordDict[i].length <= 20
s and wordDict[i] consist of only lowercase English letters.
Time: O(N^2 * M)
Space: O(N)
inputFormat: A string s and array of strings wordDict.
explanation: dp[i] is true if dp[j] is true and s.substring(j, i) is in wordDict for some j < i.

title: Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance)
problemStatement: Given two strings `word1` and `word2`, return the minimum number of operations required to convert `word1` to `word2`. You have three operations permitted on a word: Insert a character, Delete a character, Replace a character.
description: Classic Levenshtein minimum edit distance.
constraints:
0 <= word1.length, word2.length <= 500
word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters.
Time: O(M * N)
Space: O(M * N)

examples.explanation: intention -> inention -> enention -> exention -> exection -> execution.

explanation: If word1[i-1] == word2[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]).

title: Sliding Window Maximum
problemStatement: You are given an array of integers `nums`, there is a sliding window of size `k` which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. You can only see the `k` numbers in the window. Each time the sliding window moves right by one position. Return the max sliding window array.
description: Find the maximum value in every contiguous window of size k.
constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
1 <= k <= nums.length
Time: O(N)
Space: O(K)
inputFormat: An array nums and integer k.
outputFormat: An array of maximums for each sliding window.
explanation: Maintain a monotonic decreasing deque storing indices. Front of deque is always the index of the max element in current window.

title: Minimum Window Substring
problemStatement: Given two strings `s` and `t` of lengths `m` and `n` respectively, return the minimum window substring of `s` such that every character in `t` (including duplicates) is included in the window. If there is no such substring, return the empty string `""`.
description: Find the shortest substring in s that contains all characters of t.
constraints:
m == s.length
n == t.length
1 <= m, n <= 10^5
s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters.
Time: O(M + N)
Space: O(|Σ|) where Σ is alphabet
outputFormat: A single string containing the minimum window, or "".

examples.explanation: Minimum window substring "BANC" includes 'A', 'B', and 'C' from string t.
The entire string s is the minimum window.
Both 'a's from t must be included in the window. Since the largest window of s only has one 'a', return empty string.

explanation: Two pointers sliding window: expand right until window is valid (has all chars of t), then contract left to find minimal length.
